short: Using borrowed exposure makes each price change affect more virtual money.
analogy: On a longer seesaw arm, the same tilt moves the end farther.
spokenText: Leverage uses exposure larger than your own amount. Each price change affects more virtual money.

short: The teaching amount kept aside for a leveraged position.
analogy: Like a reserved cushion, it has a limit; it cannot prevent every loss.
spokenText: Margin is the teaching amount kept aside for a leveraged position.

short: A teaching rule closes the position when its equity falls to a set level.
analogy: Like a game ending at a marked boundary, not an undo button.
spokenText: A forced exit happens when the teaching rule closes the position at a set level.

short: How much and how quickly values move up and down.
analogy: Like a bus ride on a bumpy road.
spokenText: Volatility describes how much and how quickly values move up and down.

short: The fall from a previous high to a later value.
analogy: Like water level falling from its highest mark.
spokenText: Drawdown is the fall from a previous high to a later value.

short: After a loss, a larger percentage gain is needed to return; losing everything leaves no base for recovery.
analogy: If half a jug remains, returning to a full jug means doubling what remains.
spokenText: After a loss, returning to the start needs a larger percentage gain. Losing everything leaves no base for recovery.

short: Spreading exposure across different sources of risk does not remove all risk. Some can fall together.
analogy: Several baskets can still be shaken by the same bump.
spokenText: Diversification spreads exposure across different sources of risk. It does not remove all risk. Some can fall together.

short: Each percentage change applies to the amount left by earlier changes. This works for gains and losses.
analogy: Each step starts where the previous step ended, not at the original starting line.
spokenText: With compounding, each percentage change applies to the amount left by earlier changes. This works for gains and losses.

short: Charges reduce the amount left. This simplified teaching model does not include fees.
analogy: A container has less left after a small amount is taken out.
spokenText: Fees are charges that reduce the amount left. This simplified teaching model does not include fees.
